$schema-note: Hand-maintained. Data, not code: nothing under scripts/ or src/ imports this file.
tranche: R1 — the identity and tenancy REST surface on the composed root
purpose: R1 lands the FIRST business routes in `apps/core-api/src/transports`. Eight
of them, across five controllers, each reaching a published contract method.
THE ENTRY THIS LEDGER EXISTS FOR IS M05, AND IT IS THE FAILURE THAT KILLED
THREE EARLIER TRANCHES IN A DIFFERENT COSTUME. Nest reads a module's
controllers as `[...static decorator metadata, ...dynamic module metadata]`
and Express matches in registration order, so a business controller moved
from the static array into `forApplication`'s dynamic one registers BEHIND
`NotFoundController`'s `@All("{*path}")` and answers 404 for every route it
declares. Nothing about the controller changes. Its handler is still correct,
its refusals are still correct, its envelope is still correct, and the
manifest still declares the route. Only a request can see it, which is why
`route-manifest.test.ts` issues one against a process `startCoreApi` started.
M01, M02, M03, M06 AND M07 ARE THE SAME CLASS ONE LAYER UP: a route that
mounts somewhere other than where the census says it does. Each of them
type-checks, each leaves every behavioural case green, and each is a 404 in
production. They are killed by the join between the decorators' own metadata
and `operation-manifest.generated.json` — two mechanisms, two sets of surface
constants, neither of them written by the file that compares them.
M08, M15 AND M17 NEED A REAL DATABASE and are the reason this tranche has an
integration suite at all. M08 is the defect the brief names by hand — an
authorization refusal turned into a 200 with an empty list — and it is
invisible to every unit case, because the shape of the answer is valid and
only its TRUTH is wrong. M17 is the same shape one field over: `actorUserId`
where `effectiveUserId` belongs shows a support engineer their own tenant
while they believe they are seeing the customer's.
M16 IS RECORDED AS A SURVIVOR AND IS NOT PATCHED AROUND. See its entry.
procedure: Every mutation is applied to ONE file and run INDIVIDUALLY. The laptop runs
the thirteen that need no container; Docker is quit there by standing
instruction, so the three that need PostgreSQL and Redis run on the Mac mini
over ssh, in a FRESH worktree, against pgvector/pgvector:pg16 and
M13 MUTATES A GENERATOR AND MUST REGENERATE BEFORE IT MEANS ANYTHING. The
manifest is a COMMITTED artifact: editing the generator alone leaves the
committed rows untouched and every case green, which would have been a false
survivor. The driver runs `generate-control-plane.mjs` after the edit and
restores all three generated files afterwards.
M12 MUTATES A GATE THIS BRANCH DOES NOT OWN — `scripts/arch/composition-root
.mjs`'s (C8) rule — so that the BFF containment is proven by the rule going
AWAY, not by the rule agreeing with itself.

mutations.name: M05 a controller is registered AFTER the terminal 404
mutations.why: THE ENTRY THIS LEDGER EXISTS FOR. The controller is still registered, the manifest still declares the route, every unit case still passes, and every request answers TRANSPORT_ROUTE_NOT_FOUND because `@All("{*path}")` matched first.

mutations.why: Every route in the deployable moves together, so no relative assertion can see it. Only the manifest — generated from the AGENT's constants — can.
kills: × mounts exactly the method/path pairs the manifest attributes to this tree

mutations.name: M07 the process edge loses VERSION_NEUTRAL
mutations.why: `/livez` becomes `/api/v1/livez`. A liveness probe that moved on a release takes a fleet down on the next rolling restart, and nothing in the business surface notices.
kills: × keeps the process edge off the versioned surface

mutations.name: M09 an unpaged collection silently accepts a page
mutations.why: A caller who asked for five rows and received twelve, told `limit: 12`, has been answered a question they did not ask, and no status code said so.
kills: × refuses a page of an unpaged collection, naming both parameters

mutations.name: M10 the next cursor is computed instead of read
mutations.why: `offset + limit < total` and the contract's own `hasMore` agree today. The store is the only thing that knows whether another row exists, and a cursor to nothing is a client that pages forever.
mutations.from: return page.hasMore ? encodeCursor({ offset: page.offset + page.limit }) : null;
mutations.to: return page.offset + page.limit < page.total ? encodeCursor({ offset: page.offset + page.limit }) : null;
kills: × derives the next cursor from the CONTRACT's hasMore, never from arithmetic

mutations.name: M11 the guard hardcodes the cookie name
mutations.why: Over plain HTTP the hardcoded name IS the contract's answer, so the integration suite cannot see it. Only the TLS branch can: `__Host-` is a name the contract chooses and a transport is not entitled to know.
kills: × asks the CONTRACT for the name on every request, and gets a different one over TLS

mutations.name: M12 the (C8) transport containment rule is removed
mutations.guards: scripts/arch/composition-root.mjs — the rule that refuses a transport reading `app.adapters`
mutations.why: The BFF is the transport most tempted to reach past the contracts. This mutation deletes the only thing stopping it, on a branch that has just given that directory its first real controller.
kills: × C8: a bff transport reaching the canonical store through a property read with an element access fails
× C8: the SHIPPED bff controller is governed, and the reach it would make is legal without C8
× C8: the rule binds every transport, not just the bff

mutations.why: Seven routes that verify an operator session would be recorded `requiresOperator: false`, and `docs/audits/M0.8-operator-operations.md` — which exists to make operator protection auditable at a glance — would under-report them by seven.

mutations.note: Regeneration is part of the mutation. Without it the committed manifest is untouched and this would be a false survivor.

mutations.name: M14 the body reader trims what the caller sent
mutations.why: A trim is the single most innocent-looking edit in the file and it moves a domain rule into a transport: `createOrganization` refuses a blank name with TENANCY_INVALID_NAME, and a trimmed `"  "` reaches it as `""` — the same refusal, about the transport's edit rather than the caller's input.
kills: × does not trim, default or otherwise edit what the caller sent

container_mutations.name: M08 an authorization refusal becomes an empty page
container_mutations.why: THE DEFECT THE BRIEF NAMES BY HAND, and the one no unit case can see: the answer is a valid COLLECTION envelope with a valid page block, and only its TRUTH is wrong. An operator is shown an environment that appears EMPTY rather than one they may not see, and nothing on the wire, in a log, or in a screenshot distinguishes the two.
container_mutations.from: const authorization = await authorizeEnvironment(app, operator, environmentId);
container_mutations.to: try { ... } catch { return collectionEnvelope({ rows: [], cursor: null, limit: 0, nextCursor: null, total: 0 }); }
kills: × a route does not widen what the contract permits > REFUSES an unauthorized environment instead of answering an empty page
× an operator authenticates over HTTP > gives FOUR different answers to four different refusals
× impersonation > refuses the environment to the impersonated account, on the impersonated account's memberships

container_mutations.name: M15 the BFF reshapes the directive before writing it
container_mutations.why: A spread copy is the exact edit the contract's `verifySessionCookie` exists to catch: membership of the issuing register, not the shape of the value, is what it tests, so `{ ...directive }` type-checks, carries identical attributes, and is refused. This is what makes 'a BFF may only set the bytes' checkable at the seam rather than asserted in a comment.
kills: × the BFF sets bytes and nothing else > exchanges a token for a cookie the CONTRACT shaped, and the cookie then authenticates

container_mutations.name: M17 the listing keys on the actor instead of the effective user
container_mutations.guards: organizations.controller.ts — which of the two user ids reaches `listOperatorOrganizations`
container_mutations.why: Under impersonation the two ids differ, and the wrong one shows a support engineer THEIR OWN tenant while they believe they are seeing the customer's. Every other case in the suite passes: outside impersonation the two ids are equal, which is why the fixture seeds a session that impersonates.
kills: × impersonation > lists the IMPERSONATED account's organizations, not the impersonator's

survivors.name: M16 the BFF stops handing the directive back to `verifySessionCookie`
why-it-survives-and-is-kept: Nothing observable changes, and that is the honest reading rather than a
gap. `verifySessionCookie` accepts the directive the contract just minted,
so removing the round trip alters no byte on the wire and no case can see
it. It is kept because the contract says exactly what it is for: 'It does
not stop a BFF writing whatever header it likes — nothing in a process
can. It stops a MODIFIED directive being accepted back.' The value it has
is against a FUTURE edit that reshapes the directive, and M15 is that
edit: a spread copy is refused. Recording the survivor rather than
inventing a case that would pass for the wrong reason.
survivors.measured: RUN, not predicted. Applied on the mini against the real container suite (44 cases) and on the laptop against both unit suites; every case stayed green.

declared: RATE_LIMITED is not a refusal this surface can produce, and that is a
FINDING rather than a missing mutation. `consumeRateLimit` is published, but
its three actions — LOGIN, INVITE_ACCEPT, MFA_VERIFY — are all
pre-authentication credential operations, and not one of the use cases that
`acceptInvitation`) is on either published contract. A V1 route may reach a
contract method and nothing else, so there is no truthful route to spend the
budget on. A second, smaller finding sits behind it: `RateLimitRequest`
REQUIRES a `TenantScope`, and a LOGIN refusal happens before any tenant is
known. `identity-rest.test.ts` states the first as a checked claim over the
contract's own method names, so it goes red the day one is published.
